newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end higher on renewed rate cut talk.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end higher on renewed rate cut talk.

text.p: Chilean blue chips ended broadly higher in thin trade on Tuesday with the bolsa driven by fresh speculation that the Central Bank would lower interest rates, dealers said.
"Stocks have gone up basically on continued rumours of an interest rate cut," said one trader.
The bolsa is likely to retreat at the opening if the rate change fails to materialize, he added.
The 40-share index ended up 0.56 percent at 117.31 points. The general index gained 0.15 percent to 5,357.57 points.
Turnover fell to 7.6 billion pesos from 10 billion pesos Monday.
Traders said the market was likely to move in a trading range of 113-119 points until the bank lowers interest rates.
The authorities are widely expected to cut rates by 0.25 percentage points.
Electricity stocks closed firmer, although the market is jittery that continuing dry weather could lead to electricity rationing, they said.
Energy Minister Alejandro Jadresic said Tuesday that the government will decide on whether to impose rationing at the end of this month.
The drought, the worst in Chile this century, has dried dams and hurt power supplies to the country's central grid.
Winners included steel producer Cap, up 4.39 percent at 1,070 pesos, glass-maker Cristales, up 1.75 percent at 2,900 pesos and telecom Entel which rose 1.16 percent at 3,050 pesos.
Losers included drug company LabChile, down 1.56 percent at 430-1/5 pesos and telecom Telex which shed 0.88 percent at 1,120 pesos.
